findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Describe how the scan handles `--only <value>`: take the next non-flag token, remove it from argv before `parse_output`, define the error for a missing or flag-shaped value, update test_fsck_stale_channel_repair.py:109, and decide whether `--limit N` gets the same treatment.

findings.finding: AC2 says `--only <value>` and `--only=<value>` must behave the same, but the plan doesn't say how. The work is in the custom argv scan in `fsck_cli`, not in argparse. Supporting `--only <value>` means: (a) taking the following token as the value; (b) removing that token from argv before `parse_output`, because today only the flag tokens are stripped (line 362) and the leftover value would hit output parsing; (c) deciding what `--only --repair` or a trailing `--only` means; (d) changing the existing test at test_fsck_stale_channel_repair.py:109, which checks that a bare `--only` is rejected. `--limit` has the same flaw: the help shows `--limit N`, but the scan only handles `--limit=` (lines 350-356). Fixing only `--only` leaves the same help/behaviour mismatch on the neighbouring flag.
scenarios: `--repair --only stale-channel`: if the value token isn't stripped, `parse_output` rejects 'stale-channel' as an unknown argument.
`--repair --only --dry-run`: without a rule, '--dry-run' gets taken as the value of `--only`.
The `--limit 5` form is still rejected after the fix, even though the help shows it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] If the fix is help alignment, consider declaring `choices=('stale-channel',)` on `--only` in `build_fsck` so argparse renders and enforces the same value set the custom scan accepts.
evidence: repair.py:49: `parser.add_argument("--only", help="check only the named ticket(s)")` has no `choices`
fsck.py:319: `build_fsck(prog="rebar store fsck").parse_args(norm)` already checks the normalized `--only=...` against the parser
fsck.py:341: the accepted value 'stale-channel' is hard-coded separately in the custom scan
findings.finding: If the help-text branch is chosen, a simpler way to keep help and behaviour aligned is to make `build_fsck` the single source of truth with `parser.add_argument('--only', choices=('stale-channel',), help=...)`. Argparse then puts the accepted value in `--help` automatically, and `_fsck_govern` (which already runs this parser on the normalized argv) enforces the same rule. That makes help/behaviour drift structurally impossible, rather than relying on a test to keep two hand-written copies in sync. The plan should consider this, or explain why keeping the hand-written list in `fsck_cli` is better.
scenarios: Someone later adds another accepted `--only` value in fsck.py but not in the parser's help, and the two drift apart again.
findings.suggested_fix: In build_fsck: `parser.add_argument("--only", choices=("stale-channel",), help="repair only the named channel (requires --repair)")`, and in fsck_cli check against the same tuple instead of a separate string literal.
